sentences.en: Yeah, Tim Clayton and Phil Craig, but a really good, good account of the battle.
sentences.zh: 这些关于特拉法尔加海战的精彩记录，之所以如此震撼，是因为那种紧张感在数小时内不断累积。

sentences.en: These amazing accounts of the Battle of Trafalgar, and what makes them so powerful is that sense of the tension building and building and building hour after hour.
sentences.zh: 他们清理了甲板，然后是英国战舰。

sentences.en: So they clear the decks and then the British ships.
sentences.zh: 当你准备战斗时，你会把所有的家具都搬走。

sentences.en: What you do is when you're getting ready for action, you take all the furniture away.
sentences.zh: 把吊床收起来。

sentences.en: You take your hammocks down.
sentences.zh: 把吊床收起来。

sentences.en: The hammocks down.
sentences.zh: 然后把它们挂起来作为衬垫，以加固甲板侧面。

sentences.en: And you put them up to kind of serve as padding to kind of reinforce the sides of the deck.
sentences.zh: 男人们赤裸上身。

sentences.en: The men strip to the waiSt.
sentences.zh: 他们会在头上系上头带或绷带，以防止汗水流进眼睛并保护视线。

sentences.en: They sort of tie headbands or bandages around their heads so that they will keep the sweat out and protect their eyes.
sentences.zh: 他们做完这一切。

sentences.en: They do all that.
sentences.zh: 但随后仍有大量的等待时间。

sentences.en: But then there's still an awful lot of waiting.
sentences.zh: 实际上在英国战舰上。

sentences.en: And actually on the British ships.
sentences.zh: 我们开始了这一史诗篇章，我读了那首《橡木之心》（Heart of Oak）。

sentences.en: So we started this whole epic, and I read that, Heart of Oak.
sentences.zh: 那是其中的一首歌。

sentences.en: I mean, that's one of the songs.
sentences.zh: 他们唱着歌，乐队奏响了乐曲。

sentences.en: They sing, the band strikes up.
sentences.zh: 他们唱着歌，乐队奏响了乐曲。

sentences.en: Yeah, because the bands are playing.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为军乐队在演奏。

sentences.en: The bands are playing.
sentences.zh: 军乐队在演奏。

sentences.en: They sing Royal Britannia.
sentences.zh: 他们唱着《不列颠尼亚》，

sentences.en: They sing, God Save the King.
sentences.zh: 他们唱着《天佑国王》。

sentences.en: At one point, they dance the hornpipe on board.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，他们还在船上跳起了水手舞。

sentences.en: Well, also, Dominic, for breakfast, they've been given wine.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有，多米尼克，早餐时他们还分到了酒。

sentences.en: They have wine and meat.
sentences.zh: 他们有酒有肉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Wine unusually.
sentences.zh: 这很不寻常，有酒喝。

sentences.en: On Villeneuve's ship.
sentences.zh: 在维尔纳夫的船上。

sentences.en: So the British are sort of singing Royal Britannia and dancing.
sentences.zh: 所以英国人算是唱着《不列颠尼亚》在跳舞。

sentences.en: On Villeneuve's ship, I was very pleased to read that he parades the imperial eagle.
sentences.zh: 在维尔纳夫的船上，我很高兴读到他展示了帝国鹰旗。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's been given, sent by Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 那是拿破仑送来的。

sentences.en: And his officers swear oaths of loyalty.
sentences.zh: 他的军官们宣誓效忠。

sentences.en: They renew their oaths of loyalty to the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他们重申对皇帝的效忠誓言。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's the perfect British, a sort of Hogarth figure couldn't make this up.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这简直是典型的英国式场景，霍加斯的画作都编不出这种情节。

sentences.en: You know, the contrast between the sort of the high spirits of the British and the French swearing loyalty to an absolutist ruler.
sentences.zh: 你知道，英国人那种高昂的士气与法国人向绝对君主宣誓效忠之间形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: But I think there's a seaman on victory who says, you know, we are like lions anxious to be at it.
sentences.zh: 但我记得“胜利号”上有一名水手说，我们就像渴望战斗的狮子。

sentences.en: They are, they're keyed up for the battle, even though they know that lots of them are going to die.
sentences.zh: 他们确实如此，他们为战斗做好了准备，尽管他们知道自己中的许多人将会死去。

sentences.en: They seem to have a kind of battle frenzy.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎有一种战斗狂热。

sentences.en: Whereas on one of the Spanish ships, one of the captains says the fleet is doomed.
sentences.zh: 然而在其中一艘西班牙船上，一位船长说舰队注定要失败。

sentences.en: So there's a, you know, very, what is it?
sentences.zh: 所以这，你知道，非常，怎么说呢？

sentences.en: The guy from Dad's army.
sentences.zh: 就是《老爸上战场》里的那个人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We're doomed, doomed.
sentences.zh: 我们完了，彻底完了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: So anyway, so Nelson, they have this kind of, they've developed this signaling, which Nelson has been using to kind of convey orders.
sentences.zh: 总之，纳尔逊他们发展出了一套信号系统，纳尔逊一直用它来传达命令。

sentences.en: And they have this famous, Nelson wants, England confides that every man will do his duty.
sentences.zh: 他们有那个著名的信号，纳尔逊想说：英格兰相信每个人都会尽职尽责。

sentences.en: This is the message he wants to convey.
sentences.zh: 这就是他想传达的信息。

sentences.en: Confides meaning truSt.
sentences.zh: “Confides”的意思是信任。

sentences.en: So England trusts that every man will do his duty.
sentences.zh: 所以是英格兰信任每个人都会尽职尽责。

sentences.en: But they don't have a signal for confides.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有“信任”这个词的信号旗。

sentences.en: And so the signal says, could we use expects?
sentences.zh: 所以信号旗显示的是，我们能用“期望”吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so that's the message that goes up.
sentences.zh: 于是这就是发出的信息。

sentences.en: Well, 31 flags it took to signal that message.
sentences.zh: 嗯，传达这条信息用了31面旗帜。

sentences.en: And there were conflicting reports, but some say, you know, the men cheer.
sentences.zh: 虽然有相互矛盾的报道，但有人说，你知道，士兵们欢呼起来。

sentences.en: They raise a great cheer when they see this.
sentences.zh: 他们看到这个信号时发出了巨大的欢呼声。

sentences.en: Well, Collingwood, Collingwood thinks it's all a bit much.
sentences.zh: 嗯，科林伍德，科林伍德觉得这有点多此一举。

sentences.en: He complains that, you know, there are too many signals that they know what to do.
sentences.zh: 他抱怨说，你知道，信号太多了，他们本来就知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: But then he reads the signal and he welcomes it as well.
sentences.zh: 但后来他读了信号，也表示欢迎。

sentences.en: And hurrah, ready for battle.
sentences.zh: 万岁，准备战斗。

sentences.en: So slowly, slowly, slowly, the British fleet, pronged with, you know, Nelson and Collingwood, draw closer and closer and closer towards the enemy line.
sentences.zh: 于是，慢慢地，慢慢地，慢慢地，由纳尔逊和科林伍德率领的英国舰队，越来越近，越来越近，向敌方阵线逼近。

sentences.en: And a mile away, the French and Spanish start to fire.
sentences.zh: 在一英里外，法西联合舰队开始开火。

sentences.en: And the first shot flies over victory.
sentences.zh: 第一发炮弹从“胜利号”上方飞过。

sentences.en: And Nelson has two captains with him on board.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊船上有两位船长陪同。

sentences.en: And so he says, you know, chaps, time to go.
sentences.zh: 于是他说，伙计们，该走了。

sentences.en: Off you go.
sentences.zh: 你们去吧。

sentences.en: And they head off.
sentences.zh: 他们出发了。

sentences.en: And he shakes the hands of one of the captains.
sentences.zh: 他与其中一位船长握手。

sentences.en: And one of the captains takes Nelson's hand and said, I trust my lord that on my return to the victory, which will be as soon as possible,
sentences.zh: 其中一位船长握住纳尔逊的手说，我深信大人，当我回到“胜利号”时，这会尽快实现，

sentences.en: I shall find your lordship well and in possession of 20 prizes.
sentences.zh: 我将发现大人您安然无恙，并已俘获20艘敌舰。

sentences.en: On which he, Nelson, made this reply.
sentences.zh: 对此，纳尔逊作了这样的回答。

sentences.en: God bless you, Blackwood.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑你，布莱克伍德。

sentences.en: I shall never speak to you again.
sentences.zh: 我恐怕再也见不到你了。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: Biographers have had enormous, you know, spent oceans of ink about that remark.
sentences.zh: 传记作家们对此有巨大的，你知道，耗费了无数笔墨来解读那句话。

sentences.en: Does Nelson feel, you know, the Grim Reaper peering over his shoulder?
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊是否感觉到，你知道，死神在肩后窥视？

sentences.en: Does he, or is this what captains, people often say before a battle in which so many people they know will be killed?
sentences.zh: 他是这样吗？还是说这只是船长们在战斗前常说的话，因为他们知道许多熟人将会阵亡？

sentences.en: And if they live, it's a remark that will be forgotten.
sentences.zh: 如果他们活下来，这句话就会被遗忘。

sentences.en: But it lives on purely because he, I mean, who knows?
sentences.zh: 但它之所以流传下来，纯粹是因为他，我是说，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Well, so in the Victorian period where they were very agitated by his relationship with Lady Hamilton,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在维多利亚时代，人们对纳尔逊与汉密尔顿夫人的关系非常激动，

sentences.en: it became part of the myth that he felt ashamed of his relationship with Emma and was looking to re-burnish his sense of honour and was offering himself up as a sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 这成了神话的一部分，即他对自己与艾玛的关系感到羞耻，试图重塑自己的荣誉感，并主动献身作为牺牲。

sentences.en: And it is true that Nelson was obsessed with the death of James Wolfe at the Battle of Quebec in the Seven Years' War.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊确实痴迷于七年战争中魁北克战役里詹姆斯·沃尔夫的阵亡。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there was a famous painting by the American painter Benjamin West, who became president of the Royal Academy,
sentences.zh: 美国画家本杰明·韦斯特有一幅名画，他后来成为了皇家艺术学院院长，

sentences.en: who Nelson had met at Fonthill in Wiltshire, very near where I grew up, and I played cricket there.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊曾在威尔特郡的丰希尔见过他，那里离我长大的地方很近，我还在那里打过板球。

sentences.en: And Beckford was, it was owned by William Beckford, who was a kind of plantation owner, fabulously, dangerously rich, sugar baron.
sentences.zh: 贝克福德，那是威廉·贝克福德的产业，他是一个种植园主，富有得惊人且危险，是个糖业大亨。

sentences.en: And Nelson met West there and said, well, you know, why aren't you painting more canvases like the Death of Wolfe?
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊在那里遇到了韦斯特，说，嗯，你知道，你为什么不多画一些像《沃尔夫之死》那样的画呢？

sentences.en: And West says, well, you know, there aren't any heroes.
sentences.zh: 韦斯特说，嗯，你知道，现在没有什么英雄了。

sentences.en: And Nelson goes, hmm.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊说，嗯。

sentences.en: But I don't think, I mean, I think the consensus among those who studied Nelson is that he had no sense of a death wish.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为，我是说，我认为研究纳尔逊的人们的共识是，他没有求死的念头。

sentences.en: I mean, this was, he was not looking to sacrifice himself.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这并不是，他不是在寻求自我牺牲。

sentences.en: He was not looking to offer himself up as a blood sacrifice to Britain or to exonerate his shame or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 他不是在寻求把自己作为血祭献给英国，也不是为了洗刷耻辱之类的。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's a tense moment.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这是一个紧张的时刻。

sentences.en: And they are going into hell.
sentences.zh: 他们正走向地狱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's basically, we may never meet again, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 基本上就是，我们可能再也见不到了，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think so, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想是这样，是的。

sentences.en: Nelson's quite a sentimental person.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊是个相当感性的人。

sentences.en: He says very patriotic and sentimental things.
sentences.zh: 他说的话非常爱国且感性。

sentences.en: That's how I perceive it.
sentences.zh: 我就是这么理解的。

sentences.en: I don't think he's, because he thinks he's going to win.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他是，因为他认为自己会赢。

sentences.en: I mean, that's why he's devised the plan.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是他制定计划的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, he's confident he's going to win.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他有信心获胜。

sentences.en: But he also knows that he is going, as you say, going into the jaws of hell.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也知道，正如你所说，他正走向地狱的深渊。

sentences.en: And actually, it's Collingwood rather than Nelson who hits the enemy first, because the Royal Sovereign, Collingwood's flagship, has just had its hull newly coppered.
sentences.zh: 事实上，是科林伍德而不是纳尔逊先冲击敌阵，因为科林伍德的旗舰“皇家君主号”刚换了新的铜皮船底。

sentences.en: So it's very, very faSt.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常非常快。

sentences.en: Gets ahead of victory, gets ahead of the Belle Isle, which is the ship directly behind Collingwood.
sentences.zh: 它跑到了“胜利号”前面，也跑到了紧随科林伍德身后的“美丽岛号”前面。

sentences.en: So it is first into the jaws of hell.
sentences.zh: 所以它第一个冲进了地狱的深渊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Then victory as well.
sentences.zh: 然后“胜利号”也跟上了。

sentences.en: Collingwood is about two miles southeast of the victory, and the cannon fire is starting to come.
sentences.zh: 科林伍德在“胜利号”东南约两英里处，炮火开始袭来。

sentences.en: However, having said that, I think both Collingwood and Nelson know that it is not perhaps as dangerous as it might be,
sentences.zh: 然而话虽如此，我认为科林伍德和纳尔逊都知道，情况或许并没有那么危险，

sentences.en: partly because the wind and the tide and the waves are against the enemy.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是风、潮汐和海浪对敌人不利。

sentences.en: So they're rolling up and down, up and down, very difficult to get a kind of direct aim.
sentences.zh: 所以敌舰在上下颠簸，很难进行直接瞄准。

sentences.en: However, I think that neither Collingwood nor Nelson are kind of suicidally brave.
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为科林伍德和纳尔逊都不是那种自杀式的勇敢。

sentences.en: And even though the cannon fire is starting to smash into the sail, smash into the masts, all kinds of things, cannon fire is whistling paSt.
sentences.zh: 即使炮火开始轰击船帆、桅杆，各种东西，炮弹在呼啸而过，

sentences.en: They know that the swell is with them.
sentences.zh: 他们知道涌浪对他们有利。

sentences.en: So the swell is going with them.
sentences.zh: 所以涌浪在推着他们前进。

sentences.en: It's moving them forward.
sentences.zh: 它在推动他们向前。

sentences.en: But this is disrupting the ability of the French and Spanish ships to get a kind of steady aim because their ships are kind of rolling up and down, up and down.
sentences.zh: 但这干扰了法西船只进行稳定瞄准的能力，因为他们的船在上下颠簸。

sentences.en: And that means that basically, you know, it's only for a few seconds every minute that the ships are level and therefore the cannon are level.
sentences.zh: 这意味着基本上，你知道，每分钟只有几秒钟船身是平稳的，因此大炮也是平稳的。

sentences.en: And so actually the fire that is coming from the French and Spanish line is pretty irregular and very inaccurate.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上来自法西阵线的炮火相当零乱且非常不准确。

sentences.en: And on top of that, one of the technical advances that the British do have is that when they pull the trigger, it fires, whereas the French and Spanish have slow burning fuses.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，英国人拥有的技术进步之一是，当他们扣动扳机时，炮弹就会发射，而法西军队使用的是慢燃引信。

sentences.en: And that makes it even more difficult because if you're lighting a fuse that then has to kind of slow burn and the ship is rocking up and down, I mean, basically, you know,
sentences.zh: 这使得情况更加困难，因为如果你点燃的引信需要缓慢燃烧，而船只又在上下摇晃，我是说，基本上，你知道，

sentences.en: it's impossible to target your fire accurately.
sentences.zh: 你根本无法准确瞄准开火。

sentences.en: Still, I mean, it's not fun, is it?
sentences.zh: 不过，我是说，这可不好玩，对吧？

sentences.en: No, even so, the men, the crew are told to, you would generally lie flat on the deck if you're under fire, except for the officers who are not allowed to do that, basically.
sentences.zh: 不，即便如此，士兵们，船员们被告知，如果你在炮火下，通常会趴在甲板上，除了军官们，他们基本上不允许这样做。

sentences.en: So they are, you know, standing vertical targets for these whale of cannonballs that come sort of.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是，你知道，这些呼啸而来的炮弹的垂直靶子。

sentences.en: There's an unbelievably moving account from a lieutenant on the bell isle, which is the ship immediately behind Collingwood's flagship.
sentences.zh: 有一段来自“美丽岛号”上一名中尉的令人难以置信的感人描述，那是紧随科林伍德旗舰后面的船。

sentences.en: So, I mean, absolutely in the front.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，绝对是在最前线。

sentences.en: And he's, what, kind of 19, 20?
sentences.zh: 他当时，什么，大概19、20岁？

sentences.en: He wrote after the battle, seeing that almost everyone was lying down, I was half disposed to follow the example and several times stoop for the purpose.
sentences.zh: 他在战后写道，看到几乎每个人都趴着，我也有点想效仿，好几次都弯下腰去。

sentences.en: But, and I remember the impression well, a certain monitor seemed to whisper, stand up and do not shrink from your duty.
sentences.zh: 但是，我清楚地记得那种印象，某种告诫似乎在耳边低语：站起来，不要逃避你的职责。

sentences.en: Turning round, my much esteemed and gallant senior fixed my attention.
sentences.zh: 转过身，我那备受尊敬且勇敢的上级吸引了我的注意力。

sentences.en: The serenity of his countenance and the composure with which he paced the deck drove more than half my terrors away.
sentences.zh: 他那平静的神情和在甲板上踱步的从容，驱散了我大半的恐惧。

sentences.en: And joining him, I became somewhat infused with his spirit, which cheered me on to act the part it became me.
sentences.zh: 加入他之后，我受到他精神的感染，这激励我履行了应尽的职责。

sentences.en: And so that sense of being inspired by your senior officers is obviously terribly important.
sentences.zh: 所以，那种受到高级军官激励的感觉显然极其重要。

sentences.en: And that's why it's so important for Nelson that he, you know, he's prominent on the quarter deck.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么纳尔逊在后甲板上显得如此突出对他来说非常重要。

sentences.en: And that all appeals from his junior officers to him to, you know, stop making himself such an obvious target.
sentences.zh: 所有下级军官都恳求他，你知道，不要让自己成为如此明显的靶子。

sentences.en: He absolutely refuses to do it.
sentences.zh: 他绝对拒绝这样做。

sentences.en: We talked in the very first episode about the carnage and the horror of a battle like this.
sentences.zh: 我们在第一集里谈到了像这样一场战斗的杀戮和恐怖。

sentences.en: There were so many passages that I could have picked from the books we read.
sentences.zh: 我本可以从我们读过的书中选出许多段落。

sentences.en: This is one from Ben Wilson's book, Empire of the Deep.
sentences.zh: 这是本·威尔逊的《深海帝国》中的一段。

sentences.en: And he says, For thousands of sailors on both sides, the battle was a glimpse into hell.
sentences.zh: 他说，对于双方成千上万的水手来说，这场战斗是地狱的一瞥。

sentences.en: The gun deck turned into a blackened, smoky furnace.
sentences.zh: 炮甲板变成了黑烟弥漫的熔炉。

sentences.en: Men slipped on the blood and viscera of their messmates as they fought.
sentences.zh: 人们在战斗时滑倒在战友的鲜血和内脏中。

sentences.en: To continue to man the guns in these conditions required the utmost courage.
sentences.zh: 在这种条件下继续操纵火炮需要极大的勇气。

sentences.en: An officer remarked that the side effects of battle, temporary deafness and the inability to see because of the gun smoke helped
sentences.zh: 一位军官评论说，战斗的副作用，如暂时性耳聋和因炮烟而无法视物，反而有所帮助，

sentences.en: because they blotted out the noise and vision of messmates dying.
sentences.zh: 因为它们屏蔽了战友死亡的噪音和景象。

sentences.en: All the men had to keep them sane and grounded was the mechanical rhythm of loading, hauling, firing, hauling, loading over and over and over.
sentences.zh: 所有士兵保持理智和镇定的唯一依靠，就是装填、拖拽、开火、再拖拽、再装填的机械节奏，一遍又一遍。

sentences.en: But Dominic, I mean, remember, as they're approaching, they're not able to fire because they don't have a target.
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，我是说，记住，当他们靠近时，他们无法开火，因为没有目标。

sentences.en: So they are sitting ducks, basically, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上是坐以待毙，不是吗？

sentences.en: Until they can finally get to grips with the combined French and Spanish fleets when they finally pierce the line.
sentences.zh: 直到他们最终能够与法西联合舰队交火，当他们最终突破阵线时。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And the closer they get, even with the swell and the slow-burning fuses, the artillery, the cannon fire starts to generate casualties.
sentences.zh: 而且他们靠得越近，即使有涌浪和慢燃引信，炮火也开始造成伤亡。

sentences.en: So before Nelson reaches the French and Spanish line, his secretary, a man called Dr. Scott, is standing next to him, gets killed by a cannonball.
sentences.zh: 所以在纳尔逊到达法西阵线之前，他的秘书，一个叫斯科特医生的人，站在他旁边，被一颗炮弹击中身亡。

sentences.en: Well, a cannonball literally rips him in two.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一颗炮弹直接把他撕成了两半。

sentences.en: Literally.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the extent of the horror.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是恐怖的程度。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it kind of takes off his body, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以它把他的身体带走了，不是吗？

sentences.en: His kind of legs are left standing there and then they collapse.
sentences.zh: 他的双腿还站在那里，然后就倒下了。

sentences.en: Perhaps, is that poor Scott gone?
sentences.zh: 也许，可怜的斯科特走了吗？

sentences.en: Nelson asks and he gets told it is.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊问道，得到的回答是是的。

sentences.en: And also the other thing is, it's not just the cannibals, it's splinters from the wood that are kind of firing everywhere.
sentences.zh: 还有一点是，不仅仅是炮弹，木头碎片也像子弹一样到处乱飞。

sentences.en: And a splinter rips off the buckle of Hardy's shoe, which is kind of an amazing thing.
sentences.zh: 一块碎片甚至扯掉了哈迪鞋上的扣子，这简直不可思议。

sentences.en: Eight Marines get killed on the deck of victory by a single shot.
sentences.zh: “胜利号”甲板上有八名海军陆战队员被一发炮弹同时击毙。

sentences.en: And Nelson says to Hardy, you know, this is warm work, warm work to last long.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊对哈迪说，你知道，这可是场激烈的战斗，这种激战不会持续太久。

sentences.en: And he knows they've got, you know, they've got to get up close and then they can start the killing.
sentences.zh: 他知道他们必须靠近敌舰，然后才能开始杀戮。

sentences.en: And the ship that first does that is the Royal Sovereign.
sentences.zh: 第一艘做到这一点的船是“皇家君主号”。

sentences.en: A Collingwood on the Royal Sovereign closing in on the Santa Ana, which is under the command of de Alva, commanding the vanguard.
sentences.zh: 科林伍德指挥的“皇家君主号”正在逼近由德·阿尔瓦指挥的前卫舰队旗舰“圣安娜号”。

sentences.en: Adam Nicholson discussed this brilliant phrase in his book, the cold silence of the approaching British guns.
sentences.zh: 亚当·尼科尔森在他的书中探讨过这个精彩的短语：英国舰队逼近时那冰冷的寂静。

sentences.en: And the only shot that the Collingwood on the Royal Sovereign aims is a couple to create a kind of smokescreen.
sentences.zh: “皇家君主号”上的科林伍德只瞄准开了几炮，制造出一种烟幕。

sentences.en: But they still not fired a shot in anger and it glides past the Santa Ana.
sentences.zh: 但他们还没真正开火，船就从“圣安娜号”身边滑了过去。

sentences.en: Collingwood aims right, swings round and it passes under the windows of the stern of the Santa Ana.
sentences.zh: 科林伍德瞄准右侧，转舵，从“圣安娜号”的船尾窗下穿过。

sentences.en: And now the Santa Ana is absolutely at its most vulnerable and Collingwood can rake the Santa Ana.
sentences.zh: 现在“圣安娜号”处于最脆弱的状态，科林伍德可以对它进行侧舷扫射。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's able to rake it basically for about a minute as it drifts paSt.
sentences.zh: 它在漂流经过时，基本上能进行长达一分钟的扫射。

sentences.en: So a minute of just constant hell coming from the guns of the British ship, just ripping through the Santa Ana basically.
sentences.zh: 所以，那一分钟里，英国军舰的火炮不断倾泻着地狱般的火力，几乎把“圣安娜号”撕成了碎片。

sentences.en: Because as I said, if you're aiming at the ribs of a ship, the side of a ship, you can't get through.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我所说，如果你瞄准船的肋骨，也就是船侧，你是打不穿的。

sentences.en: But if you're aiming at it, it's kind of like a kind of soft, it's open.
sentences.zh: 但如果你瞄准船尾，那里就像是敞开的，比较柔软。

sentences.en: You can aim artillery fire and it will go through all the decks right the way to the front of the ship.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接进行炮击，炮弹会穿过所有甲板，一直打到船头。

sentences.en: And so that minute that the Royal Sovereign is drifting past the stern of the Santa Ana, 240 of a crew of 800 are killed in the space of a minute.
sentences.zh: 所以，在“皇家君主号”漂过“圣安娜号”船尾的那一分钟里，对方800名船员中有240人丧生。

sentences.en: And that is the impact of kind of close impact gunnery.
sentences.zh: 这就是近距离炮击的威力。

sentences.en: That is the condition of chaos that Nelson has wanted to create.
sentences.zh: 这就是纳尔逊想要制造的混乱局面。

sentences.en: I mean, imagine the scene, Tom, the smoke, the, I mean, literally people's heads, body parts flying through the air, splinters.
sentences.zh: 我是说，想象一下那个场景，汤姆，烟雾，还有，字面意思上，人们的头颅、身体部位在空中飞舞，还有木屑。

sentences.en: I mean, splinters would kill an enormous number of people, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 我是说，木屑会杀死大量的人，对吧？

sentences.en: It's awful, awful.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了，太可怕了。

sentences.en: It's absolute, it's absolute chaos, absolute carnage.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是彻底的混乱，绝对的屠杀。

sentences.en: Obviously, the moment that the Royal Sovereign has drifted past, more and more French and Spanish ships are kind of coming up, like, I suppose,
sentences.zh: 显然，在“皇家君主号”漂过去之后，越来越多的法国和西班牙船只涌了上来，我想，

sentences.en: like kind of bees in a hive that's been disturbed.
sentences.zh: 就像蜂巢被捅了之后的蜜蜂一样。

sentences.en: They're firing muzzle to muzzle, hugely playing to the British advantage.
sentences.zh: 他们进行着面对面的炮战，这极大地发挥了英国人的优势。

sentences.en: I mean, lots and lots of British sailors are dying, but they're losing maybe 25%.
sentences.zh: 我是说，虽然有很多英国水兵阵亡，但他们的损失率可能只有25%。

sentences.en: The French and Spanish are losing 50%.
sentences.zh: 而法西联军的损失率高达50%。

sentences.en: And that's the margin of victory.
sentences.zh: 这就是胜利的差距。

sentences.en: Well, this is an interesting thing, because this is that Nelson knew, and the whole strategy was based on the fact that the British gunnery was quicker, more effective,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有意思，因为纳尔逊很清楚这一点，整个战略都基于这样一个事实：英国的炮术更快、更有效，

sentences.en: more efficient.
sentences.zh: 效率更高。

sentences.en: So they know that as many as they are losing, if they're still firing, they will inflict more damage on the enemy than the enemy can ever possibly inflict on them.
sentences.zh: 所以他们知道，尽管他们也在损失人手，但只要他们还在开火，他们对敌人造成的伤害就远超敌人对他们造成的伤害。

sentences.en: So essentially, those British casualties are the payment for the opportunity to force a surrender.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，那些英国人的伤亡是换取迫使敌方投降机会的代价。

sentences.en: So by quarter past two in the afternoon, Santorana has surrendered.
sentences.zh: 因此，到了下午两点一刻，“圣安娜号”投降了。

sentences.en: So the strategy is bloody, it's brutal, it costs a lot of British lives, it costs even more lives, French and Spanish lives.
sentences.zh: 所以这个战略是血腥的、残酷的，它牺牲了许多英国人的生命，也牺牲了更多的法国和西班牙人的生命。

sentences.en: But as far as the British is concerned, it works.
sentences.zh: 但就英国而言，它奏效了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the head of the other line, victory, has reached the enemy.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，另一条战线的领头舰“胜利号”也抵达了敌阵。

sentences.en: It aims first at the Santissima Trinidad, the largest ship in the world, with its four decks, and then for the Boussantour, Villeneuve's flagship,
sentences.zh: 它首先瞄准了世界上最大、拥有四层甲板的“圣三位一体号”，然后是维尔纳夫的旗舰“布森托尔号”，

sentences.en: with the eagle that has been given to it by Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 上面还有拿破仑赐予的鹰旗。

sentences.en: Again, it rakes the Boussantour's stern, just as Collingwood had done, Nelson kills hundreds within that kind of, you know, that minute of concentrated lethal fire.
sentences.zh: 同样，它扫射了“布森托尔号”的船尾，就像科林伍德做的那样，纳尔逊在那一分钟集中的致命火力中杀死了数百人。

sentences.en: Victory itself gets raked through its brow, and that's the moment that kills more people on board victory than any other.
sentences.zh: “胜利号”自己也被扫射了，那一刻是“胜利号”上伤亡最惨重的时刻。

sentences.en: That's by the French ship Neptune, or Spanish ship.
sentences.zh: 那是法国军舰“海王星号”干的，或者是西班牙军舰。

sentences.en: That's right, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，是的。

sentences.en: French ship Neptune, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是法国军舰“海王星号”，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: A ship called the Redutable, commanded by a very, very brave, tough captain called Jean-Jacques Lucas, blocks off victory's passage.
sentences.zh: 一艘名叫“敬畏号”的军舰，由一位非常勇敢、强硬的舰长让-雅克·卢卡斯指挥，挡住了“胜利号”的去路。

sentences.en: So victory's essentially stationary, and there's a kind of piece of iron that gets caught and essentially solders victory and Redutable together,
sentences.zh: 所以“胜利号”基本上动弹不得，有一块铁钩住了两艘船，把“胜利号”和“敬畏号”焊在了一起，

sentences.en: so that the guns are just kind of firing away.
sentences.zh: 于是火炮就在那里不停地轰击。

sentences.en: Because otherwise, the force of the blast would have propelled victory away from Redutable, but it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 因为如果不这样，爆炸的冲击力本会把“胜利号”推离“敬畏号”，但它没有。

sentences.en: And this essentially is what dooms Nelson, because Lucas and his men are desperate to board victory.
sentences.zh: 这基本上注定了纳尔逊的命运，因为卢卡斯和他的手下拼命想要登上“胜利号”。

sentences.en: But even though they can't do that, they're absolutely packed with musket men.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们没能做到，但船上挤满了火枪手。

sentences.en: And Lucas, recognising that he can never outgun the British gunners,
sentences.zh: 卢卡斯意识到他永远无法在火炮上胜过英国炮手，

sentences.en: he locks up the portholes so that it gets harder for the British cannonballs to get through and relies on his muskets, his musketry, his soldiers.
sentences.zh: 于是他封死了炮眼，让英国人的炮弹更难打进来，转而依靠他的火枪、火枪手和士兵。

sentences.en: And that means a lot of musket balls firing.
sentences.zh: 这意味着大量的火枪弹在射击。

sentences.en: And 1.15 in the afternoon, probably, I mean, I don't know, maybe you'd say that the arrow that killed King Harold at Hastings is the most famous shot fired in British history.
sentences.zh: 下午一点十五分，可能，我是说，我不知道，也许你会说在黑斯廷斯战役中杀死哈罗德国王的那支箭是英国历史上最著名的一枪。

sentences.en: This is up there.
sentences.zh: 这一枪也名列其中。

sentences.en: This is certainly up there, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这绝对名列其中，不是吗？

sentences.en: Probably first equal.
sentences.zh: 可能并列第一。

sentences.en: The shot is fired that hits Nelson, and he falls on his left side right into the blood where John Scott had been killed.
sentences.zh: 那一枪击中了纳尔逊，他倒向左侧，正好倒在约翰·斯科特阵亡后留下的血泊中。

sentences.en: And he gets drenched in Scott's blood.
sentences.zh: 他浑身都被斯科特的血浸透了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the decks are covered in sand to soak up the blood.
sentences.zh: 甲板上铺着沙子用来吸血。

sentences.en: And it's a measure of how much, you know, just how much carnage had been left by the destruction of Scott's upper body.
sentences.zh: 这足以衡量斯科特上半身被炸碎后留下了多少血腥。

sentences.en: The blood drenches Nelson.
sentences.zh: 鲜血浸透了纳尔逊。

sentences.en: And he cries out, they've done for me at laSt.
sentences.zh: 他大喊道：他们终于干掉我了。

sentences.en: And Hardy, who's standing next to him, says, I hope not.
sentences.zh: 站在他旁边的哈迪说：我希望没有。

sentences.en: And Nelson says, yes, my backbone is shot through.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊说：不，我的脊梁骨被打穿了。

sentences.en: So he's fallen, he's been, the musket ball has hit him in his left shoulder, gone through the epaulette, and it's picked up fragments of fabric as it passes.
sentences.zh: 他倒下了，火枪弹击中了他的左肩，穿过肩章，在穿透过程中带入了一些布料碎片。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it goes down through his chest, severs an artery, I think round about his lung, and then lodges, it smacks into his backbone and lodges in his spine.
sentences.zh: 它穿过他的胸膛，切断了一条动脉，我想是在肺部附近，然后卡住了，它撞进他的脊椎并留在那里。

sentences.en: And the force of it knocks him down onto his knees and men cluster around him.
sentences.zh: 冲击力使他跪倒在地，人们围了上来。

sentences.en: Take him below deck.
sentences.zh: 把他抬到甲板下。

sentences.en: And, yeah, so they, they realize he's got to go below deck straight away to the surgeon's cockpit.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们意识到他必须立刻被抬到甲板下的外科医生手术室。

sentences.en: Four of them take him down the ladders.
sentences.zh: 四个人把他抬下了梯子。

sentences.en: I mean, just imagine how unbelievably agonizing that must have been.
sentences.zh: 我是说，想象一下那该有多么难以忍受的痛苦。

sentences.en: Well, and to be carried down these ladders.
sentences.zh: 而且还要被抬着下这些梯子。

sentences.en: And Nelson, of course, had lost his arm.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊当然已经失去了一只手臂。

sentences.en: It had been operated on.
sentences.zh: 他之前做过手术。

sentences.en: And one of the things that he specified before Trafalgar is fought is that the surgeons below deck should warm up their knives.
sentences.zh: 他在特拉法尔加海战前特别交代过一件事，就是甲板下的外科医生应该把手术刀加热。

sentences.en: Yes, as he remembered the chill of the iron.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他记得那种冰冷铁器的触感。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Tom, I think we should take a break on this, at this climactic moment, and then come back after the break to talk about what happens to Nelson and what happens in the battle.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，我想我们应该在这个高潮时刻休息一下，休息后再回来谈谈纳尔逊的结局以及战斗的后续。

sentences.en: In the battle.
sentences.zh: 战斗的后续。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 几分钟后见。

sentences.zh: 大博弈。

sentences.zh: 英国与俄罗斯之间的战略斗争。

sentences.zh: 总理，我们以高度的信心评估，那是。

sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人干的。

sentences.zh: 他们击落了一架载有350人的英国客机。

sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫的那个人在玩火，亚历克斯。

sentences.zh: 你得问问自己，你想玩还是不想玩？

sentences.zh: 你是总理。

sentences.zh: 你什么都没做！

sentences.zh: 我们需要了解政策背景。

sentences.zh: 今天所有相关的背景都将构建成一个框架。

sentences.zh: 并分发成作战命令。

sentences.zh: 或者叫碎片化命令。

sentences.zh: 一个要求刺杀俄罗斯总统的碎片化命令。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: Goalhanger出品。

sentences.zh: 谁能完成这个任务？

sentences.zh: 你是我的士兵，对吧？

sentences.zh: 汤姆·麦克达夫中士。

sentences.en: Duffy.
sentences.zh: 达菲。

sentences.zh: 一场独一无二的音频剧之旅。

sentences.en: Men like Duffy.
sentences.zh: 像达菲这样的人。
